nodes.label: ref-extractor Subagent
nodes.rationale: One-subagent-per-PMID extraction judgment (study-type classification, PICO+ normalization) that a deterministic script cannot perform; scripts only validate/commit its JSON output.

nodes.label: ref-synthesizer Subagent
nodes.rationale: N retrieved evidence candidates -> one grounded answer; PLAN.md names exactly two subagents (ref-extractor, ref-synthesizer) and no others are invented even where a task (e.g. citation checking) doesn't perfectly fit either.

nodes.label: RoB 2 Risk-of-Bias Checklist
nodes.rationale: 5-domain RCT risk-of-bias tool; most domains legitimately resolve to insufficient_information because the phase-4 claim schema captures PICO+outcome data, not methodological-quality signals like randomization concealment or blinding -- an honest limitation, not a module shortfall.

nodes.label: Newcastle-Ottawa Scale
nodes.rationale: 3 star-rated categories (selection, comparability, outcome/exposure) for cohort/case-control studies; only partially assessable from claim-schema fields.

nodes.label: AMSTAR-2 Checklist
nodes.rationale: A representative subset of AMSTAR-2's 16 items (not all) applied to meta-analyses via regex signal-matching on evidence_span text.

nodes.label: GRADE Certainty Rating
nodes.rationale: Cross-paper (set-level) certainty rating, downgraded from an RCT/non-RCT baseline by risk-of-bias, inconsistency, imprecision, and indirectness factors; publication bias is always not_assessed for a curated single-library snapshot; this rating is NOT per-PMID so it has no corrections.json review home, unlike per-paper appraisal domains.

nodes.label: Freeze/Refresh Manifest Contract
nodes.rationale: A saved selector-scoped artifact (export batch, comparison table, brief, appraisal review) never silently changes membership underneath its conclusions: re-running with the same batch/key label and no --refresh reuses the frozen resolution; --refresh re-resolves and reports added/removed/changed items against the prior freeze. Explicitly shared across export.py, compare.py, brief.py, and appraise.py's run_review, each cross-referencing the others in their docstrings.

nodes.label: studies.jsonl (study grouping records)
nodes.rationale: Grouping PMIDs into a study is never automatic (not from shared authors or dataset) -- a human/agent must assert it with confidence + evidence, since correlated papers are not thereby the same investigation.

nodes.label: datasets.jsonl (dataset identity records)
nodes.rationale: Dataset reuse is a separate relationship from study grouping: two papers reusing the same dataset are not thereby the same study.

nodes.label: One-paper vs multi-paper: uniform code path over resolution["pmids"]
nodes.rationale: build_candidates() and run_summarize() operate uniformly over resolution["pmids"] regardless of length so a one-paper set degrades to a single-paper summary through the same code path rather than a special-cased branch.
nodes.norm_label: one-paper vs multi-paper: uniform code path over resolution["pmids"]

nodes.label: ref-synthesizer subagent
nodes.rationale: Reused unchanged from agents/ref-synthesizer.md because its contract ('N retrieved evidence candidates -> one grounded answer') is already generic enough to fit summarize's fixed-instruction narrative task, following the precedent /ref:check-citations set in phase 7 for judgment tasks PLAN.md doesn't name a dedicated agent for.

nodes.label: corrections.json overlay record
nodes.rationale: Six target types (claim, concept_mapping, person_identity, grant_link, author_contribution, appraisal) share one corrections.json record shape per paper for audit symmetry across all review decisions.

nodes.label: grant_link review never folds award_number into approved_aliases
nodes.rationale: Normalization is funder-specific and MUST NOT collapse distinct awards without a reviewed rule; review_grant_link records the link but never calls grant.py's add_alias itself -- folding requires an explicit separate step so distinct award numbers stay distinct unless someone deliberately says otherwise.
nodes.norm_label: grant_link review never folds award_number into approved_aliases

nodes.label: author_contribution flags require explicit evidence, never inferred from position
nodes.rationale: Shared-first, shared-senior, and corresponding authorship are independent flags requiring explicit contribution/correspondence evidence; review_author_contribution refuses without a non-empty evidence_statement, with no default and no inference from last author position.
nodes.norm_label: author_contribution flags require explicit evidence, never inferred from position

nodes.label: Vision description caching keyed by (figure hash, model, prompt)
nodes.rationale: Vision descriptions are selective (requested during promotion or for a question) and cached per figure by hash+model+prompt so identical requests never re-invoke the vision model; the script itself never calls a vision model -- it only manages the cache and figure metadata, leaving actual image interpretation to the calling multimodal agent.
nodes.norm_label: vision description caching keyed by (figure hash, model, prompt)

nodes.label: Vision output labeled model_interpretation, separate from reported results
nodes.rationale: D17: vision descriptions are stored as a sibling `vision` list on the figure entry, never merged into `caption`, and explicitly kind: model_interpretation so a figure description is never mistaken for an author-reported finding.
nodes.norm_label: vision output labeled model_interpretation, separate from reported results

nodes.label: Extraction tiers
nodes.rationale: Promotion only goes up; having full text is a separate fact from tier so acquisition never silently inflates or deflates extraction confidence.

nodes.label: Relations & edges
nodes.rationale: potential_conflict is the only auto-proposed edge type; contradicts requires explicit human review with rationale so disagreements are never silently escalated.

nodes.label: Corrections overlay lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Corrections are appended, never edited in place, and flip to pending_review when underlying evidence changes, so human judgment is preserved as an auditable overlay rather than mutating raw extraction.

nodes.label: Studies, datasets, methods
nodes.rationale: Kept as three separate registries because a shared dataset does not prove two papers report the same study; only explicit create-study groups papers.

nodes.label: Identifier contract
nodes.rationale: Three identifier classes (slugs, citekeys, opaque IDs) keep user-facing names collision-refused while machine IDs stay unambiguous; citekeys are the one exception that gets a suffix so manuscripts never break.

nodes.label: Selector grammar
nodes.rationale: One shared selector grammar resolves to a frozen PMID set copied into every artifact manifest, so a saved comparison or brief never silently changes membership on rerun.

nodes.label: Claim v2 (phase 12)
nodes.rationale: Cited claims stay searchable pointers but never count as evidence, so only a paper's own results support graph edges.

nodes.label: Ontology (phase 13)
nodes.rationale: Auto-apply is restricted to exact alias or MeSH-ID reuse; everything else becomes a reviewed proposal to prevent silent concept merges.

nodes.label: Evidence profile (phase 14)
nodes.rationale: Reports components, an independence range and a band rather than a single 0-100 score, since a single number would falsely imply precision the underlying evidence doesn't support.

nodes.label: Paper directory anatomy
nodes.rationale: Immutable raw snapshots, versioned derived records, and user-owned files are kept in separate zones so regeneration can never overwrite raw evidence or your own annotations.

nodes.label: Papers handoff (asymmetric export)
nodes.rationale: Outbound is files-only and inbound is reads-only because Papers' live database's actions_queue is a sync queue that writes could corrupt; highlights have no outbound path since they're anchored to Papers' own file copy.

nodes.label: Ingest & commit (figure 2)
nodes.rationale: A per-PMID lock serializes writes to one paper while a short-lived library lock only guards citekey allocation, so one paper's failure or slow write never blocks another paper's ingest.

nodes.label: Full-text acquisition (figure 3)
nodes.rationale: fetch.py tries sources in a fixed priority ladder (JATS, Unpaywall, publisher HTML, plain text, abstract-only) and stops at the first applicable rung, so acquisition never silently mixes source quality.

nodes.label: Extraction fan-out (figure 4)
nodes.rationale: One ref-extractor subagent per PMID runs in parallel and commits independently, so one paper's malformed claim never blocks or corrupts another paper's extraction.

links.description: The icon's central visual element is an orange furry mascot character with glasses, reading a book, on a rounded-square teal/dark-teal gradient background, with sparkle accents and a stack of books beside it.
icon-128.png is the app/plugin icon for the claude-ref-manager project.
The reading mascot with books visually connotes reference/reading material management, aligning with the project's purpose as a reference manager.
